\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{واقعیت} (vâqe'iyat)}{واقعیت (vâqe'iyat)}]{\fa{واقعیت} (vâqe'iyat) — a fact; reality}

\label{lesson:FA-C364-vaqeiyyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be proven, then the Persian for evidence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{واقعیت}}
\textbf{\fa{واقعیت}} (\emph{vâqe'iyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fact; reality\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{یک} \fa{واقعیت} \fa{است،} \fa{نه} \fa{یک} \fa{نظر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in yek vâqe'iyat ast, na yek nazar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is a fact, not an opinion.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{vâqe'iyathâ}. \emph{Dar vâqe'} \textquotedblleft{}in fact\textquotedblright{} shares its base.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{واقعیت}} is built on Arabic \emph{wāqi'} \textquotedblleft{}happening, real\textquotedblright{} with the abstract ending \emph{-iyat}; it is usually traced to Arabic \emph{wāqi'iyya} \textquotedblleft{}reality\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vâqe'iyat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vâqe'iyat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{vâqe'iyat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be proven, then the Persian for evidence, then say \emph{vâqe'iyat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حقیقت} (haqiqat)}{حقیقت (haqiqat)}]{\fa{حقیقت} (haqiqat) — the truth}

\label{lesson:FA-C364-haqiqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for evidence, then the Persian for a fact.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حقیقت}}
\textbf{\fa{حقیقت}} (\emph{haqiqat}) — \textquotedblleft{}the truth\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بالاخره} \fa{حقیقت} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{گفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bâlâkhare haqiqat râ be mâ goft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end she told us the truth.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar haqiqat} — in truth. Plural \emph{haqâyeq}, an Arabic broken plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{حقیقت}} comes from Arabic \emph{ḥaqīqa} \textquotedblleft{}truth, reality\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from the same Arabic family as \emph{ḥaqq} \textquotedblleft{}right, true\textquotedblright{}, the source of Persian \emph{haq}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haqiqat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haqiqat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{haqiqat}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for evidence, then the Persian for a fact, then say \emph{haqiqat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{واقع} (dar vâqe')}{در واقع (dar vâqe')}]{\fa{در} \fa{واقع} (dar vâqe') — in fact, actually}

\label{lesson:FA-C364-dar-vaqe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fact, then the Persian for the truth.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{واقع}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{واقع}} (\emph{dar vâqe'}) — \textquotedblleft{}in fact, actually\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{واقع} \fa{او} \fa{برادر} \fa{من} \fa{نیست،} \fa{پسرعموی} \fa{من} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dar vâqe' u barâdar-e man nist, pesar'amu-ye man ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In fact he is not my brother; he is my cousin.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} + \emph{vâqe'} \textquotedblleft{}real\textquotedblright{}. It corrects or sharpens what came before, and takes a whole clause.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{واقع}} joins the inherited Persian preposition \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} to \emph{vâqe'}, usually traced to Arabic \emph{wāqi'} \textquotedblleft{}happening, real\textquotedblright{}: in what really happens.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar vâqe'}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar vâqe'}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dar vâqe'}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a fact, then the Persian for the truth, then say \emph{dar vâqe'} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{در} \fa{واقع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In fact, actually\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شایعه} (shâye'e)}{شایعه (shâye'e)}]{\fa{شایعه} (shâye'e) — a rumour}

\label{lesson:FA-C364-shayee}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the truth, then the Persian for in fact.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شایعه}}
\textbf{\fa{شایعه}} (\emph{shâye'e}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rumour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{فقط} \fa{یک} \fa{شایعه} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in faqat yek shâye'e ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is only a rumour.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{shâye'ât} or \emph{shâye'ehâ}. \emph{Shâye'e dorost kardan} — to start a rumour.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{شایعه}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{shā'i'a} \textquotedblleft{}hearsay, rumour\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), literally something that spreads.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انکار} \fa{کردن} (enkâr kardan)}{انکار کردن (enkâr kardan)}]{\fa{انکار} \fa{کردن} (enkâr kardan) — to deny}

\label{lesson:FA-C364-enkar-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for in fact, then the Persian for a rumour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انکار} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{انکار} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{enkâr kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to deny\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{همه} \fa{چیز} \fa{را} \fa{انکار} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u hame chiz râ enkâr kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He denied everything.
\end{quote}

\emph{Enkâr} \textquotedblleft{}denial\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan} (stem \emph{kon-}). The object takes \emph{râ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{انکار}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{inkār} \textquotedblleft{}denial\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); joined to the inherited Persian verb \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, it makes a compound verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for in fact, then the Persian for a rumour, then say \emph{enkâr kardan} again
\end{itemize}
